title: Drift a sprung splice plate into line, bolt it, then swap the drift for the last bolt
instruction: Bolt the blue splice plate to the grey flange through both holes. Use the drift pin, then stand it back in its holder.
context: Structural iron and steel workers line up connection holes with a drift pin, bolt the free holes, then knock out the drifts and bolt those holes too (O*NET 47-2221.00 Structural Iron and Steel Workers; 49-9044.00 Millwrights do the same on machine bases). Holes that do not line up by hand are normal in fit-up, and the drift's taper does the moving. Board pin tasks (pin-fit, aligning two pipe flanges and pinning them) seat a pin in holes that are already in line; here the tool must make the line against a spring, and the drift may come out only after another bolt holds it.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); z is height above the table top. Table: oak-coloured top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. Flange: fixed, centred at x 27, y 0: two dark steel legs 12 x 1.5 x 6 cm (y -11.75 and +11.75) under a grey steel plate 12 x 25 x 2 cm (z 6 to 8), with two slotted holes 3.0 (x) by 3.6 (y) cm at y -8 (hole A) and +8 (hole B), open below. Splice plate: blue steel, 10 x 22 x 1.5 cm (z 8.03 to 9.53), 120 g, sliding along y on the flange (friction 0.3) against a 150 N/m spring that holds it 2.9 cm toward -y from where its holes would sit over the flange's. Its two slotted holes (3.0 x 3.6 cm) are at y +-7.7 in its own frame, 0.6 cm closer together than the flange's. At rest a 1.0 cm strip of hole A and a 0.4 cm strip of hole B show through the plate. Travel: 0.3 cm toward -y and 3.4 cm toward +y of rest. Drift pin: orange steel, 100 g, hanging by its head: head 4.0 x 2.9 x 4.0 cm, shank 2.0 x 2.9 x 2.0 cm, then a 4.0 cm taper that narrows in y from 2.9 to 0.3 cm (6 cm below the head in all). Bolts: two, yellow steel, 80 g each: head 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.0 cm, a grip tab 4.0 (x) x 1.8 (y) x 3.0 cm on top, and a 1.6 x 1.6 cm shank 6 cm long whose last 1 cm is chamfered to 1.3 cm. Holders: three fixed dark steel collars, each 6.5 cm tall with a 3.2 cm square opening and 1 cm walls (5.2 cm square outside); a part hangs by its head on the rim with its tip 0.5 cm above the table, so its top is 10.5 cm up: drift at x 19, y -16.5; one bolt at x 19, y -24.5; the other at x 19, y +17.
scoring: Open both grippers first. J is how far the plate has slid from rest (ruler). Drift in hole A: its tip below the plate, within 2 cm of the hole axis, tilted at most 15 degrees. Bolt home: shank through the flange (tip 5 mm or more below its underside), head's underside within 4 mm of the plate top, tilted at most 5 degrees, axis within 1.2 cm of a hole axis. 0.25: at some time the drift stood in hole A with J of 1.4 cm or more for 1 s. 0.5: also a bolt is home that was put there while the drift was in a hole. 0.75: also both holes have a bolt home. 1.0: also the drift stands in its holder (head's underside within 1 cm of the rim, tilted at most 10 degrees, centred within 1.5 cm) and every part is still. A part off the table, or a bolt home with no drift line made: 0.
reset_notes: Let the spring push the plate back to rest. Hang the drift and both bolts by their heads in their holders. Nothing is consumed or bent. In a real trial keep fingers off the plate edges and out of the holes while the plate is under spring load.
fidelity: Rigid-body approximation: the plate is a damped sprung slide on a fixed flange, the holes are boxes, and the drift taper is two tilted slabs. Bolts are not tightened and no torque is modelled. The simulator scores the last step with the grippers still closed, so a part whose underside is more than 1 cm above its seat counts as not placed. The pinch rule for fingers is a real-trial rule the scorer cannot see.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached toward the holders with both arms, never lined up the plate or placed a bolt); demo: 1.0 (right arm drifted the plate into line, both bolts went in, drift returned to its holder)
